title: Five haunted Milwaukee locations and the stories behind them
excerpt: From theaters to a library, and even an old brewery, these places in Milwaukee have a history of ghost stories.
content:
Oct. 30, 2026, 5:02 a.m. CT

Milwaukee was founded way back in 1846, meaning more than enough to time has passed for the city to collect a few ghost stories.

From shadowy figures to unexplained voices, the Journal Sentinel put together a list of Milwaukee destinations with rumors of haunted happenings, from theaters to a library, and even an old brewery.

Here are five reportedly haunted places around Milwaukee.

Pfister Hotel

Milwaukee's Pfister Hotel has had more than a few reports of ghostly encounters over the years, most notably among visiting athletes.

In 2013, Former Los Angeles Angels pitcher C.J. Wilson was staying there and using his one night when the lights began to flicker. Then, the lights shut off, and the TV.

But the lights came back on and Wilson went about his day – until he heard a scratching noise from inside the walls.  

“Now I'm thinking, 'OK, it's the Midwest. There could be a possum or something in the wall, right? That's possible, isn't it?'” Wilson said. “All I knew was that there were definitely noises coming from the wall." 

By now, the supposed hauntings at Pfister Hotel have been widely reported. More than a few baseball players have talked about other odd occurrences. In 2016, then-Los Angeles Angels first baseman Ji-Man Choi said he felt the presence of a spirit in his bed.  

David Ortiz recently said he would rather not stay there because of the hotel's supposedly haunted happenings.

Noah Leigh, founder and lead investigator at Paranormal Investigators of Milwaukee, said there are also stories centered around the ghost of Mr. Pfister and hot spots at the towers that were put in the 1960s. Guido Pfister and his son, Charles, opened the hotel in 1893. It's a member of the Historic Hotels of America.

Paranormal Investigators of Milwaukee is a nonprofit that has checked out dozens of spots with five investigators.

Old Pabst Brewery  

Jim Haertel, owner of Best Place at the Historic Pabst Brewery, was with a paranormal investigation team at the old Pabst Brewery location near Fiserv Forum. The team was checking for ghostly activity, and they did so by unscrewing flashlights to the point where the circuit wasn’t connected enough to light the bulbs up.  

That all changed when the team welcomed the supposed ghosts into an old jail cell they were investigating. Slowly, the lights turned on and off multiple times.  

“That was probably one of my scarier moments here,” Haertel said.  

He said he used to consider himself a skeptic, but too many strange things have happened. There have been reports of children's voices when no children are around, or unexplained shadows in the office of Captain Pabst, with smoke sometimes purportedly seen in the area due to his love of cigars.

Pabst's ship, the Comet, was known along the western shores of Lake Michigan. He married the daughter of a brewer in Milwaukee and eventually bought half the Phillip Best Brewing Company, which would be renamed to Pabst Brewing Company.

The building has generated so many haunted stories that Haertel now runs ghost tours.  

Paradise Theater  

Leigh said his team caught suspicious audio when it investigated the old Paradise Theater in 2010. The West Allis theater has since been sold and is now a church, but the investigation captured some unexplained noises, including what sound like voices saying "hey" and the name "Lydia."

The supposedly haunted audio is posted online. The investigators hope to return at some point because even with that audio, there isn't really enough evidence to say the building is haunted, Leigh said.

Shadows have been seen walking around near the projector room bathroom, figures have appeared and disappeared in front of staff, and seats will mysteriously get pushed down when nobody is there, he said.  

Milwaukee Central Library  

The Paranormal Investigators of Milwaukee team has checked out Milwaukee Central Library before.  

There are stories about a woman who jumped to hear death from the second floor, Leigh said, and she can supposedly still be seen standing at the window. A custodian also once saw a door close by itself when it is only supposed to open with a code.  

Other reports include papers shuffling and an old grandfather clock going off by itself. The rare books room is even said to be haunted by a deceased local author who has books there.

The paranormal investigators weren’t able to verify any of claims when they visited.

Riverside Theater  

An employee used the restroom one day in part of the Riverside Theater building only open to staff when a figure suddenly appeared. That worker went to go track them down to ask them to leave, but the figure left the bathroom, went down the hallway and over to a balcony.

By the time the employee caught up, the figure was gone, Leigh said.  

Other reported hauntings have been reported in the laundry room and the light booth, he said.
